name: Vodafone Group Plc

profile.description: Vodafone is a pan-European and African telecommunications group providing mobile, fixed broadband, and business digital services, with leading positions in Germany, the UK (following the merger with Three UK), Turkey, and — through Vodacom and now fully consolidated Safaricom — sub-Saharan Africa, including the M-Pesa mobile money platform. FY2026 (to March) revenue was about €40.5B, and Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.7% to €10.3B with 5.2% organic service revenue growth and a 28.5% adjusted EBITDAaL margin. CEO Margherita Della Valle, a long-time Vodafone executive and former CFO, has run the company since 2023 and has exited Spain and Italy to simplify the portfolio. Market cap approximately $36.8B.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on the Dividend sleeve (12 weight units) [4]. D/E of 100.2% scores 0.87; ROE of 0.1% scores 0.01; profit margin of -1.0% scores 0; forward P/E of 9.5 scores 1.0 [4]. Revenue growth uses Q1 FY27's 9.7% (Yahoo's YoY field was unavailable), scoring 0.99, and the 5yr revenue CAGR of -1.4% (FY2021 €43.8B to FY2026 €40.7B per FMP, depressed by the Spain and Italy disposals) scores 0.24 [1][5]. Dividend metrics: payout ratio of 102.6% scores 0; 12+ consecutive years paid per yfinance history scores 1.0 at 2x weight; 0 years of growth after the 2025 cut; and a derived 5yr dividend CAGR of -12.7% (current $0.54 annual rate vs. $1.06 paid in 2021) scores 0 at 2x weight [4]. Weighted result 4.26/10 rounds to 4. Liquidity passes: 3.62M avg volume x $15.88 = ~$57.5M/day.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Under Della Valle, Vodafone sold Spain and Italy and merged its UK unit with Three, a major portfolio reshaping, but these are consolidation moves rather than new products [2]. AI Deployment (1/2): Vodafone signed a $1.5B AI partnership with Microsoft and plans to sell AI and cybersecurity services to businesses; business digital services are growing at high double digits, but no AI-specific revenue or savings are quantified [1][2]. Market Share (1/2): The Three UK merger and Safaricom consolidation strengthen scale, but Germany is losing ground to mobile competition, growing just 1.2% [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Management is targeting business customers at ~50% of group revenue in the medium term, but without dated product launches [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D is reported separately, typical of telecom operators [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Vodafone's purpose — connecting for a better future through technology that improves lives, livelihoods and the planet — is clear and links connectivity to inclusion, but peers such as Deutsche Telekom and Orange use very similar language [3]. Community Impact (1/2): Vodafone's African mobile money and financial services, including M-Pesa through Vodacom and Safaricom, extend financial access, but no distinctive dollar-quantified philanthropic program surfaced in this research [1]. Employee Retention (0/2): MSCI flags labour management as almost 25% of Vodafone's rating and a source of higher risk in Europe, and no retention data were found [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider transaction data were available for the U.S.-listed ADR.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Vodafone owns licensed spectrum, mobile towers, and fixed networks across Europe and Africa — regulated physical infrastructure that AI cannot replace, and AI workloads add data traffic [1]. Some exposure exists in customer service and in enterprise IT services, where Vodafone competes with hyperscalers to sell AI and cloud services [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Vodafone is selling AI and cybersecurity services to businesses and reports high double-digit digital services growth, but discloses no AI-specific revenue figure [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: Vodafone sits at the low end of Sinek's MIXED zone. Della Valle's simplification — exiting Spain and Italy, merging in the UK, cutting the dividend to fund the network, and pushing into business digital services — shows willingness to accept short-term pain [2]. But the purpose language is generic for the industry, the restructuring was driven by years of underperformance, and the competitive narrative in Germany is about defending share.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Connecting for a better future' is a sincere purpose statement and is partly lived through African financial inclusion, but it is interchangeable with peers and did not prevent a decade of value-destroying sprawl [1][3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong — Della Valle is a long-tenured Vodafone insider promoted from CFO — but MSCI flags labour management as a meaningful risk in Europe, suggesting average rather than exceptional trust [2][3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management framing in Germany centers on competitive pressure in mobile and defending share; no commentary framing rivals as a source of improvement was found [1].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The pivot toward business digital services (SaaS, IoT, cloud, security, AI) and African fintech is a meaningful evolution, though the company remains fundamentally a telecom operator [1][2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Della Valle exited Spain and Italy and roughly halved the dividend in 2025 to reinvest and repair the balance sheet — decisions that cost income investors and reported scale in the short term [2][4].

investment_thesis: Vodafone's restructuring is starting to show up in growth. Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.7% to €10.3B and organic service revenue grew 5.2% with every segment contributing, adjusted EBITDAaL grew 6.2% organically with margin up 0.6 points to 28.5%, and management raised FY27 guidance to €13.0-13.3B adjusted EBITDAaL and €2.6-2.9B adjusted free cash flow, now expecting the upper end [1]. Business service revenue growth accelerated to 5.0% on high double-digit growth in SaaS, IoT, and cloud and security, and Africa grew 12.6% organically, with Safaricom fully consolidated from July 1, 2026 [1]. At 9.5x forward earnings with a 3.4% yield and a Yahoo Finance PEG of 0.59, the shares price in little of that recovery [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is Germany and the balance sheet. Germany, the largest market, grew only 1.2% organically amid mobile competition, and the UK just 0.6% [1]. FY2026 was another statutory loss (-€0.40B net income after a €1.8B tax charge, per FMP), Yahoo Finance shows ROE of 0.1% and D/E near 100% on €54B of debt, and the payout ratio exceeds 100% of trailing earnings [4][5]. The dividend was roughly halved in 2025 and is far below 2021 levels (a derived -12.7% 5yr CAGR), and FY2026 revenue of €40.7B remains below FY2021's €43.8B after the Spain and Italy exits [4][5]. MSCI cut its ESG rating to A from AA, with labour management contributing almost 25% of the rating [3].
key_catalysts: H1 FY27 results in November 2026 confirming the raised €13.0-13.3B EBITDAaL guidance and upper-end free cash flow [1]
Safaricom full consolidation from July 1, 2026 and continued double-digit Africa growth in connectivity and M-Pesa financial services [1]
Three UK merger synergies and business digital services (SaaS, IoT, cloud and security, AI) moving business customers toward the CEO's medium-term goal of ~50% of group revenue [1][2]
key_risks: German mobile competition holding Germany organic growth to 1.2% and pressuring the group's largest earnings contributor [1]
Leverage and weak statutory returns: ~€54B of debt, D/E ~100%, ROE ~0.1%, and a payout ratio above 100% of trailing EPS leave limited room for dividend growth [4]
Execution risk on the UK merger integration and on monetizing AI and cybersecurity services in the enterprise market against hyperscalers and IT services firms [2]
